answer: Continuous memory-bandwidth leasing requires every registered agent to stream verifiable random reads across a 32 GB local RAM buffer that is continuously overwritten by the river state root. Because the whisper verifier checks sub-millisecond read latency against a per-ID seed, two identities cannot time-share one DRAM bus or fetch pages over a network link without exceeding the eight-millisecond timeout and getting dropped from the trellis routing table. Every extra fake forces the operator to buy and power another physical memory channel, scaling hardware outlay linearly with headcount.
